A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multilingual synthetic-data study. Their main text, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably, including v3's added Appendix A.13.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and downstream fine-tuning experiments across eleven languages and three tasks, with F1 results, sample-size analyses and rejection rates.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a pilot model comparison, performance-similarity correlation and data-diversity measurements.

M1.justification: The seven generation configurations, summarized-label prompting, demonstrations, revision procedure, four generating LLMs and final XLM-R pipeline remain unchanged. The added explanations and reported mBERT pilot do not establish a change to the final method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same eleven languages, MASSIVE intent-recognition subset, SIB-200 topic classification and sentiment datasets. The new diversity and correlation analyses concern retained data and tasks.

E2.justification: Section 3 newly reports a pilot comparison with mBERT, stating that XLM-R achieved better average scores, without providing numerical pilot results. The generation-strategy comparisons and gold-data comparator in the main evaluation remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds n-gram diversity evaluation of gold and generated training data, aggregated across languages in Table 13. Existing sampling and downstream training settings are retained; early stopping with patience five was already documented in v1 Appendix A.6.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds analyses testing whether similarity predicts downstream F1 and whether generated data increase diversity. v1 only suggested the diversity explanation. Existing sample-size sensitivity, revision and similarity analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 adds Pearson correlation estimation between downstream performance and similarity to human data. Ten-run/ten-seed reporting and Figure 4's 95% confidence intervals remain unchanged; no additional runs or new significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing F1 scores and rejection rates are unchanged. New findings include average Pearson correlation 0.111 and generated-minus-gold diversity differences of +0.218 for intent recognition, +0.581 for sentiment and -0.279 for topic classification (Section 5, Table 13), plus the qualitative XLM-R-over-mBERT pilot result.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. The added empirical metrics introduce no mathematical definitions, formal assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same scope and principal claims about target-language demonstrations, revision, model-size differences and small performance gaps to gold data in selected settings.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges missing human quality annotations and unknown pretraining-data contamination, including possible effects on language/domain comparisons. It also connects the new sentiment-diversity findings to dataset heterogeneity, expanding the existing interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 documents same-label pairwise averaging for embedding similarity, synthetic development-data provenance and XLM-R's size and language support. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, prompt templates and code/data-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Devlin et al. (2019) for the newly reported mBERT pilot comparison. The related-work discussion and positioning around the lack of comparative generation-strategy evaluations for low-resource languages remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose additions and edits, supplies explanatory cross-references beneath previously bare appendix headings, and adds A.13. It also corrects the first author's surname from Ankinina to Anikina. The overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 13, places Figures 4 and 5 together on one page, and repositions appendix tables. Existing figures and table structures are retained; the changes primarily concern the added display and placement.

improvement.justification: Section 5 and Table 13 provide empirical follow-up to v1's diversity speculation, while clearer computation details and explicit human-validation and contamination limitations improve transparency. These are useful, limited gains: the mBERT pilot lacks numerical results, and the n-gram diversity metric remains insufficiently specified for reproduction.
